members.name: Future members of Public Image Limited

podcast.title: Pre-Clash Band
podcast.body: The London SS was Mick Jones's band before The Clash, known for a "rotating line" of members. Despite managing to rehearse sometimes, they "never really got around to actually playing a gig." The group included future members of bands like Generation X and Public Image Limited, and notably featured Chrissie Hynde, who would later form The Pretenders. Joe Strummer agreed to join the band just as it broke up, leading to the formation of The Clash with Mick Jones.

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Unplayed Gigs
podcast.body: This band is described as "the most famous British punk band to never play a gig." Despite many people, including Chrissie Hynde, flowing through its lineup, "nothing really happened with the London SS," which merely possessed "promise and potential." "The Clash evolved out of the most famous British punk band to never play a gig. They were called the London SS."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Evolution from London SS
xref.body: The Clash evolved out of a prominent British punk band known as the London SS, which was famous for never playing a gig. Many musicians passed through London SS, including Chrissie Hynde, who later formed The Pretenders. "The Clash evolved out of the most famous British punk band to never play a gig. They were called the London SS."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Origins and Formation
xref.body: The Clash originated from a "stillborn" group called the London SS. They officially formed in late 1976 within a severely dilapidated squat located on Davis Road in West London. Their manager was a used car salesman. "The clash evolved out of a stillborn group called the London SS."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
